sources.citation: Wikipedia. Yeyi language (wikitext, downloaded 2026-09-17).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Calls Yeyi tonal (citing Gunnink 2023); phoneme tables from Seidel 2008; no stress statement. Used for bibliography leads (Donnelly 1990 = UCT BA Hons thesis; Baumbach 1997; Gowlett 1997).

sources.citation: Gunnink, H., N. Chousou-Polydouri & K. Bostoen. 2025. Yeyi: A phylogenetic loner in Eastern Bantu. Languages 10(4): 55. doi:10.3390/languages10040055
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress and tone (lexical phylogeny; mentions clicks and Seidel 2008 pp. 101-129 for sound changes).

sources.citation: Gunnink, Hilde. 2023. Vowel harmony in Yeyi. Studies in African Linguistics 52 (Suppl. 13): 99-120.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about stress; p. 101: tone is contrastive, many sources inconsistent, refers to Seidel 2008 prosodology. Also notes Seidel (2008: 49) restricts front vowel harmony to the penultimate syllable (p. 110).

sources.citation: Gunnink, Hilde. 2022. Morphological Khoisan influence in the Southern African Bantu language Yeyi. JALL 43(1): 3-35. doi:10.1515/jall-2022-8892 (Ghent green-OA postprint)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress and tone (morphology paper).

sources.citation: Lusekelo, Amani. 2009. Review of Frank Seidel 2008, A Grammar of Yeyi. Afrikanistik online 2009: 1-5. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2009_3531
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Second-hand summary of Seidel 2008 ch. 2: phonemes/phonotactics/syllable pp. 27-53, prosodology pp. 54-99; High tone = Prosodeme II, Low tone = Prosodeme I, semantically distinct (p. 57), grammatical functions (p. 61), plus Prosodeme III; intonation 'demarcative and expressive'. No mention of stress.
